c.tagline: Riverside capital of lush Casamance, gateway to Diola villages and the beaches of Cap Skirring.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hail apps in Ziguinchor — agree the fare before setting off. Shared taxis and cars rapides (painted minibuses) run fixed routes for a few hundred francs; hiring a taxi for yourself costs more.

emergency.note: 17 reaches the police and 18 the sapeurs-pompiers (fire and rescue); 1515 is the SAMU medical line. Mobile coverage of these lines can be patchy outside the city.

avoid.reason: Casamance region — occasional separatist activity and rural landmines; check advisories

hood_desc: The compact commercial heart on the Casamance River, around the market, the pier where pirogues land and the gare fluviale; the walkable base where most hotels, banks and restaurants sit and everything is within 20 minutes on foot.
The old African quarter of low tin-roofed houses and lively street life, the traditional cultural core of the town with local eateries and a strong Diola and Mandinka character.
A residential district of shaded compounds and family homes just back from the centre, quieter and local, with small guesthouses and neighbourhood cafés.
A calmer residential and guesthouse area on the town's edge, popular for cultural immersion and longer stays, with easy pirogue access to the mangroves.
A leafy riverside stretch of faded French-colonial villas and the town's better hotels, with gardens and views over the Casamance River; the quietest, most scenic base.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.hours: Shared taxis and cars rapides run from around dawn until early evening; after dark, chartered taxis are the main way to get around.
transit.note: Ziguinchor has no formal public transport network; getting around means shared yellow taxis and cars rapides (painted minibuses) on the main roads, plus pirogues from the gare fluviale for river trips.
transit.pay: Pay the driver or conductor in cash (a few hundred CFA francs a hop); there is no transit card. Carry small notes.

bus: Sept-place shared taxis & buses to Dakar (via The Gambia)
Cars rapides / minibuses around town and to Cap Skirring
ferry: Pirogues on the Casamance River and to the mangroves

transit.m: Taxi to the city centre (5-10 min)
Shared taxi / minibus toward the centre

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving ~10% at restaurants and for guides is appreciated but not expected.
